newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Palm sees large EMU starting in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Palm sees large EMU starting in 1999.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Tuesday that European monetary union would be likely to begin on schedule in 1999 with a large group of nations, including Germany.
"I presume that it is likely for monetary union to start in 1999," Palm told Reuters in an interview.

He added that a postponement of the start would be dangerous for Germany but added that it, like most other EU nations, already met three out of four of the core criteria for single currency union entry.
He noted however that it was too early to say whether Italy would be in at the time.
Palm, also head of the state bank of Baden-Wuerttemberg, said a postponement of EMU would cause more problems than it would solve.
"A postponement is no solution for existing problems," Palm said, adding that for Germany a delay could raise the danger of an overvaluation of the mark.
Currently Germany and a number of other nations already met three out of the four criteria on inflation, long-term interest rates and foreign exchange levels, he said.

Palm also said there was no worry that Germany would miss meeting deficit goals as long as it stuck to its savings course. "A majority of nations are all able to reach the criteria as long as they save assiduously," he said.
He predicted that the so-called deutschemark block -- Austria, Ireland, the Benelux nations and France -- would all be among the first nations to join the currency union.

Asked whether Italy might also be among the first group, he said: "It is very pleasing that so many nations want to participate in EMU but too soon to say whether Italy will be among the first nations.
